accessibility: Each menu opens from its button with the keyboard and closes with Escape; the member chip's name carries the nickname, kind and label; the collapsed destinations keep their names as accessible names and the collapse button names its action.
The sidebar is a named region containing a primary and a secondary navigation; the diagnostics count carries its words, never a number alone.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Rail, NavItem, Stack, Text, Icon, Button, ListItem, Divider, Badge, TextInput, Alert, SegmentedControl, Segment, TabBar and TabBarItem); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog. The shell is the one of the Overview View.

The menus are Stack cards of ListItems placed under their control, as in Canvas: Render context and zoom bar; the collapsed sidebar is a second Rail with the collapsed layout swapped in by a Variant, because a Rail cannot collapse itself on desktop; the tablet and phone forms are the responsive layouts of the same Widgets.
The strings of the app are copied under the same Locale keys; the diagnostics count of a View in the navigator is sample content.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A signed-in member is on a page of the Workbench; the navbar and the sidebar are the shell's. The page below them is the Overview, drawn as in Overview & readiness; the View navigator is what the sidebar shows on a View page.

The base state is the expanded sidebar with both menus closed. Variants open one menu below the control it belongs to, show the notices a menu action raises, collapse the sidebar to its 56px icon rail and show the View navigator.

The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the Workbench chrome follows the Workbench language, so its text is baked here per Locale. The member, the revision and the View names are sample content.
spec.intent: Show the two menus of the Workbench navbar, the Workspace mark and the signed-in member, and the sidebar in its collapsed and its View-navigator states, as built from Adapter Widgets only.
interactionRules: The Workspace mark opens a menu that identifies the Workspace (Local Workspace) and copies its revision; it never switches Workspaces, because one server serves one. A copy says Copied, and one the browser refuses says so.

The member chip shows the nickname, the label and, in its menu, the member's kind and label with Sign out; a member who holds the manage-members key also sees Members, and others see no Members entry. Signing out says so and returns to the sign-in page.

On desktop a button at the foot of the sidebar collapses it to the icon rail and back, and remembers the choice; each destination keeps its name as a tooltip and an accessible name. Tablet always shows the icon rail, and expanding opens the full sidebar over the canvas; on a phone the bottom bar replaces the sidebar.

On a View page the sidebar lists the Widget layers of the View, and All Views switches to a filterable list of the Views, each with its feature tag and the count of its diagnostics, the View open marked; a filter that matches nothing names what was typed.
